risk.rationale: I rated it medium. The feature is read-only and shows no amounts. It does consume two new endpoints (E-PROJECTS, E-PROJECT), and the frontend must honour INV-ACCESS through "no grant: 404" without leaking the project title. It also changes the shared contract mock (`frontend/mock/server.mjs:24`, 226-234) while F-05, F-06 and F-08 change the same file (PMO-0-3), and it replaces a route that the frame tests assert on (PMO-0-4). Surfaces: - `ui`: SCR-22 and SCR-07. - `api`: the first reads of E-PROJECTS and E-PROJECT through the generated client and the mock. Excluded surfaces: - `payments`: the Money and Milestones tabs are split out. - `contract-change`: no repoint and no openapi edit. - `security` and `auth`: the page only renders 401, 403 and 404 through the existing mapping. - `product-decision`: the omitted elements are recorded for product acceptance, not decided here.

findings.summary: An opaque `case_id` containing reserved characters is encoded twice. `/projects/P%2F..%3Cb%3E` sent `GET /api/v1/projects/P%252F..%253Cb%253E`, because Next hands the route param already encoded and openapi-fetch encodes it again. Expected: one level of encoding, so the backend sees the same id the URL carried. Actual: the id the server decodes is `P%2F..%3Cb%3E`. Real ids are uuids (REC-CASE), so there is no impact today, and the mock falls back to the default journey for unknown ids. The fix is to decodeURIComponent the segment before the client call, in `frontend/src/features/projects/useProject.ts` or the route page. Check this when FE-CONNECT-1 meets the real API.

The proposal shapes the client reads are not type-guarded and differ from the v7 draft. Today they only reach the page from the mock, so nothing breaks. Once a backend serves v7, `ProjectsList.tsx:97` (`item.next_milestone ?? '—'`) would render an object `{name, due}` as a React child and throw. `ProjectJourney.tsx:117` would print "PM [object Object]" because v7 `pm` is `{name, role, is_you}`. v7 `facts` is an array of `{label, value, money, unknown}`, but the client reads an object, so the strip shows "Not known". v7 `summary` is `agent_summary` `{agent, text}`, and the line `tone` and `station` are new. The client should check `typeof` before rendering each proposal field (string for `next_milestone`, `pm` and the line text), so that an unexpected shape degrades to "—" or "Not known" instead of throwing. When v7 is frozen, align `model.ts` and the mock fixtures to it. Under the standing rule this does not block the round.

findings.summary: The Active tab sends `status=active` by default (`model.ts` `buildProjectsQuery`). A v6 backend does not know this parameter. If it ignores it, the "Active" tab shows every project, closed ones included, with no marker. If it rejects unknown query parameters, the list shows the error card. The client does not filter and shows no status, so it cannot tell. Please record this as a coordination point with the backend developer, or send `status` only when the page has seen `counts` (which the list cannot know before the first read).
